sections.html:
The Recorder sits in the Administrative Courthouse at 210 East Main Street, Suite 205, in Lancaster. Weekday hours run 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, and you can call 740-652-7100. Everything that becomes part of the county's permanent public record lands here, including deeds, mortgages, leases, liens, plats, powers of attorney and military discharges.

The land records index goes back to 1800, and scanned documents can be searched online from January 1980 on. Employees will tell you which desk to visit. They will not do your searching, help write a document or give you recording forms, so the deed itself comes from a closing agent or an attorney.

  • Look up deeds and mortgages through the land records link on the Recorder page.
  • The same page has free sign-ups for a Property Fraud Alert and a Notary Fraud Alert.
  • Phone ahead before a trip. Short closures, such as a one-hour midday closing on a single day, get posted on that page.

Take the deed to the County Auditor before the Recorder. The transfer is completed there, and the recording step comes afterward. Most sales need two papers at the Auditor: the deed, plus a conveyance fee statement on Ohio form DTE 100 (DTE 100EX if an exemption applies).

The Auditor's Map Room compares the legal description with county conveyance standards before accepting the deed. You can email a prepared deed to the Map Room for that approval, and the transfer cannot proceed without it. After approval, leave the deed and statement at the transfer desk, 108 N. High Street in Lancaster, or mail the set to the Auditor marked Attn: Conveyance.

Ohio puts the statement of value on the buyer or the buyer's representative, and the conveyance fee on the seller. Value is everything paid or promised for the property, and that includes the mortgage. A gift is valued at its estimated open market price. R.C. 319.202 prohibits knowingly writing a false value.

You will pay two separate bills. One is the Auditor's transfer and conveyance charges. The other is the Recorder's fee, which grows with the number of pages.

Fees on a Fairfield County deed
ChargeRatePaid to
Transfer fee$.50 per parcel, exempt and non-exempt transfers alikeCounty Auditor
Conveyance fee$4.00 per thousand of consideration when money changes handsCounty Auditor
Recording, first two pages$17 base fee plus $17 housing trust fund feeCounty Recorder
Recording, each added page$4 base fee plus $4 housing trust fund feeCounty Recorder
Document preservation surchargeUp to $5, if the county charges itCounty Recorder

The figures follow the Auditor's conveyance fact sheet and Ohio Revised Code 317.32. A fee schedule is linked from the Recorder page, and it is the place to check the surcharge and any other line item before writing a check. R.C. 322.02 also lets a county add a real property transfer tax of up to 30 cents per $100, paid by the grantor at the Auditor ahead of recording.

sections.h2: Who can acknowledge a deed, and where it is filed
sections.html:
An Ohio deed needs the grantor's signature, acknowledged in front of an authorized officer (R.C. 5301.01). Acceptable officers are:

  • a judge or clerk of a court of record in Ohio
  • a county auditor or county engineer
  • a notary public
  • a mayor

Record in the county where the land lies. R.C. 5301.25 treats an unrecorded deed as fraudulent against a later good faith buyer with no knowledge of it. A house in Pickerington, Canal Winchester, Reynoldsburg or an unincorporated township is still recorded in Lancaster.

Each instrument is entered in the order presented, stamped with date and exact time. R.C. 317.13 gives the Recorder room to turn away anything materially false or fraudulent. A person who is refused may petition the Court of Common Pleas for an order to record.

Yes. Simplifile is the e-filing route the Auditor's fact sheet names. Someone filing only once may find the account setup more trouble than it is worth and can simply file on paper.

State law pushed every county recorder, auditor and engineer toward electronic recording of conveyances, with recorders posting online indexes and images for instruments recorded since January 1, 1980. Fairfield's own online start in 1980 fits that. Logins are allowed for viewing, though no charge for a login is.

If you choose paper, ask your title company whether it would rather submit electronically for you. Many closing agents already hold a Simplifile account, which means the deed can be sent the same day it is signed and you avoid a trip to Lancaster altogether.

Paper still works. Deliver the deed to the Auditor, then pay the Recorder's fee. Phone 740-652-7100 to arrange return of the original.

sections.h2: Before you close on a Fairfield County sale
sections.html:
Lancaster is both seat and largest city of Fairfield County, which belongs to the Columbus metropolitan area and counted 158,921 residents in 2020. Franklin, Licking, Perry, Hocking and Pickaway counties border it. A neighboring county's mailing address does not move the recording location. Before you list, check with the city or township office for open permits on the house.

Three offices are involved, so keep a short closing checklist: approve the legal description, sign the conveyance fee statement, confirm taxes with the Treasurer, then record.

  • Legal description cleared by the Auditor's Map Room
  • Grantor's signature acknowledged by an authorized officer
  • Statement of value (DTE 100 or DTE 100EX) completed
  • Transfer and conveyance fees paid at the Auditor's transfer desk
  • Recording fee sent to the Recorder

Selling for cash removes the lender's paperwork, yet each item above still applies. Your title company normally sequences the stops. You bring your signature, a photo ID for the notary and your latest tax bill. If a mortgage is being paid off, expect the release to be recorded as well, and ask the title agent when that filing will be done.

sections.h2: If you suspect fraud on your property
sections.html:
Fraud on a house is rare, but it hurts most when the owner is away, the home is empty or the owner has died. Inherited houses waiting for a sale are a common target, so sign up before you list.

Start by enrolling in the Recorder's free alerts, which notify you of new documents recorded under your name or a notary's name. If something looks wrong, phone 740-652-7100 to ask what was filed, then talk to an attorney. Veteran ID cards are issued by this office as well, through the same number.

Keep your closing documents in one folder after the sale. A recorded deed and the matching release of any old mortgage are your proof that the title is clear, and you may be asked for them again.

faqs.q: Which office files a deed for a Fairfield County house?
faqs.a: The Recorder, at 210 East Main Street, Suite 205 in Lancaster, once the County Auditor has processed the transfer. The Auditor is a separate stop at 108 N. High Street.

faqs.q: What does the Auditor charge to transfer a deed in Fairfield County?
faqs.a: A $.50 per parcel transfer fee, plus a conveyance fee of $4.00 per thousand of consideration when money changes hands. Have the transfer desk confirm the total before you bring payment.

faqs.q: Does Fairfield County have its own deed form?
faqs.a: No. Neither forms nor drafting help come from the Recorder. A title company or attorney writes the deed, and the Auditor's Map Room reviews the legal description.

faqs.q: Can I look up old Fairfield County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Partly. The index reaches back to 1800, but images are online only from January 1980 forward. Older documents are viewed at the office.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee when a house sells?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor. The buyer files the statement of value with the Auditor.
